spoken: Univariate, one variable, every view that matters.
Change the bins, or the data range.
Change the bins, or the range. The chart and the statistics update.
Outliers.
The lower plot drops values beyond the fences.
I Q R is selected. Red points are flagged.
Kernel density.
Kernel density draws a smooth curve through the same observations.
A smaller bandwidth multiplier redraws that curve.
Q Q and P P.
The Q Q plot uses a normal reference.
The lower plot is the detrended residual from the reference line.
Distribution sets the reference.
Normality.
Normality is assessed from six different normality tests.
The gauge is the normality strength index, a combined proprietary index from those six tests. It shows how strongly the sample tends toward normality. Here it reads 66.
Confidence interval.
Classical and bootstrap are offered. Bootstrap is for a parameter with no closed analytical solution, such as the median.
Confidence rises from 95 percent to 99 percent, and the interval widens from 6.5 to 8.6 horsepower.
Bootstrap is clicked, and the median is selected. The center moves to 196.5. The interval turns uneven: 9.2 below, and 10.8 above.
Hypothesis test.
First, run the test. The null mean is 200 horsepower.
Run the Test is clicked.
P-value 0.916. The test fails to reject.
Visualize is clicked, yellow marks the statistic, and red marks rejection.
The null is 185. Clicked again, it rejects.
Power Analysis is clicked. The required size is 139.
